claim: A TinyML speech-recognition model deployed on ESP32 via Edge Impulse's EON Compiler achieved 87.14% test accuracy with 266 ms real-time inference latency.
stance_target: feasibility of real-time on-device speech/voice-command recognition on low-cost microcontrollers for ECE embedded projects
scope_conditions: curated subset of Google Speech Commands Dataset, ESP32 microcontroller, Edge Impulse tooling
quoted_support: The final model attained 87.14% accuracy on testing data and 97.1% average classification confidence during real-time inference, with excellent noise rejection (99.6%) and latency of 266 ms.

claim: Quantization/optimization via Edge Impulse's EON Compiler reduced RAM usage by 37% and ROM usage by 27% for the deployed speech-recognition model.
stance_target: quantization as an effective resource-reduction technique for deploying ML models on ultra-low-power microcontrollers
quoted_support: Using Edge Impulse's EON Compiler, the model was fully quantized and optimized, achieving a 37% reduction in RAM usage and 27% in ROM.

claim: On-device TinyML speech recognition on ESP32 is positioned as competitive with cloud-dependent ASR systems while reducing latency, power consumption, and bandwidth requirements, making it suitable for battery-powered IoT, robotics, and embedded automation.
stance_target: TinyML/edge-AI as a viable ECE project direction over cloud-based speech recognition
quoted_support: Compared to state-of-the-art systems deployed on more powerful platforms, the proposed approach achieves competitive accuracy while maintaining real-time inference and minimal resource consumption on ultra-low-power hardware.
